title: Foundation — Full Gym
subtitle: Machine and cable base-building circuit
coaching_note: Machines are the right call here — they let you push effort without worrying about stabilizing a free weight while the pattern is new. Set the seat/pad height before you start each machine; a bad setup makes every rep worse.

exercises.name: Treadmill Brisk Walk / Light Jog
exercises.form_cue: Build from a walk to a light jog over the five minutes. You should be able to talk in short sentences by the end.
exercises.why: Raises core temperature and heart rate before you load any machine.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.form_cue: Arms straight, pull the band apart until it touches your chest, squeeze your shoulder blades.
exercises.why: Activates the upper back before pressing movements ask it to stabilize.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.form_cue: Feet shoulder-width on the platform. Lower until your knees hit about 90 degrees, don't let your lower back round off the pad.
exercises.why: Builds quad and glute strength with the machine handling balance, so you can focus purely on range and control.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.form_cue: Pad sits just above your heel. Curl through the full range, pause a beat at the bottom.
exercises.why: Direct hamstring work most beginner programs skip — keeps the front and back of the thigh balanced.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.form_cue: Wide grip, lead with your elbows down and back, pull to your upper chest. Don't lean back to muscle it down.
exercises.why: Builds the back strength that a straight-arm cable movement teaches better than free weights at this stage.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.form_cue: Handles at chest height, press straight out without locking your elbows out hard at the top.
exercises.why: Guided path lets you push real effort into the chest and triceps without a spotter.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.form_cue: Chest up, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
exercises.why: More pulling volume to keep pushing and pulling balanced — most desk-bound bodies are pull-deficient.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.form_cue: Set the pulley high, pull the handle diagonally across your body to the opposite hip, rotate through the torso not just the arms.
exercises.why: Trains rotational core strength — most sports need force to transfer across the body, not just forward.

exercises.name: Foam Roll: Quads and Lats
exercises.form_cue: Slow passes, pause on any tender spot for a few seconds.
exercises.why: Loosens what you just loaded before you leave the gym.

progression_notes: Once all three sets land at the top of the rep range with a clean last rep, bump the stack up one increment. Move from machine chest press to dumbbell bench press once machine press feels easy for two sessions running.
